items.title: IRGC offers Hormuz passage to nations that expel US, Israeli envoys

featured_image.name: Navy 'tracks' Iranian ships with unmanned systems in Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Monday offered passage through the Strait of Hormuz, starting Tuesday, to any Arab or European country that expels Israeli and U.S. ambassadors from its territory, according to Shafaq News. The proposal marks a new front in Tehran's diplomatic pressure campaign as its war with the United States and Israel enters a second week.[1]

items.title: UC San Diego study finds most pandemics show no lab origins

featured_image.name: Scientists discover key clue in pandemic viruses that reveal if they were made in a lab... including Covid and 'Russian flu'

items.description: Two studies published in the past week offer fresh perspectives on viral threats — one revealing how coronaviruses rewire human cells to speed their own replication, and another providing a genomic tool to distinguish natural outbreaks from lab-linked ones, with new molecular evidence that the 1977 "Russian flu" pandemic likely originated from a failed vaccine trial.

items.title: Trump calls Iran's choice of Mojtaba Khamenei 'a big mistake'

featured_image.name: Worst-case scenario': Trump weighs replacing Khamenei as ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday sharply condemned Iran's selection of Mojtaba Khamenei as its new supreme leader, telling NBC News that the country "made a big mistake" and casting doubt on whether the appointment would endure. "I don't know if it's going to last ... I think they made a mistake," Trump said in a phone interview.[1][2]

In a separate interview with the New York Post, Trump said he was "not happy" with the 56-year-old cleric replacing his father. "Not going to tell you. I'm not happy with him," Trump said from his Doral golf club near Miami when asked about his plans regarding the younger Khamenei.[3][4]

items.title: Iran says it does not want to harm 'ordinary Americans'

featured_image.name: An interview with Iran's foreign minister

items.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Monday that Tehran does not wish to harm ordinary American citizens, framing the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict as a war driven by Israel and its allies in Washington rather than a quarrel with the American public.

"Iran does not want to harm ordinary Americans who overwhelmingly voted to end involvement in costly foreign wars," Araghchi wrote in a post on X. "Blame for surging gas prices, costlier mortgages, and pummeled 401(k)'s lies squarely with Israel and its dupes in Washington."[1]

items.title: Trump doesn't rule out seizing Iranian oil as prices spike

featured_image.name: Trump says buying Iranian oil must stop, threatens secondary ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday declined to rule out the possibility that the United States could seize Iranian oil as the war against Tehran enters its second week, telling NBC News that "certainly, people have talked about it" while stopping short of endorsing such a move.[1][2]

"People have thought about it, but it's too soon to talk about that," Trump said, pointing to Venezuela as a precedent where the U.S. moved to secure oil access after American forces captured President Nicolás Maduro in January. Trump touted the Venezuela operation during last month's State of the Union address, saying the U.S. had already obtained more than 80 million barrels of Venezuelan oil.[2]

items.title: Trump and Putin discuss Iran and Ukraine in phone call

featured_image.name: Two-hour Trump-Putin call ends without ceasefire

items.description:
President Donald Trump called Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday to discuss the war in Iran and ongoing efforts to settle the conflict in Ukraine, according to the Kremlin, in what appears to be the first direct conversation between the two leaders since reports emerged that Russia has been sharing targeting intelligence with Tehran against American forces.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters that Trump initiated the call "to discuss a number of critically important topics related to current developments in the international situation," with the conversation focused on the Iran conflict and trilateral negotiations on a Ukraine settlement. Ushakov described the exchange as "businesslike, frank and constructive" and said the two presidents "have not spoken by phone for a long time and agreed to communicate with each other on a regular basis".[1][2]

items.title: Iran confirms new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei wounded in war

featured_image.name: Mojtaba Khamenei wounded after surviving assassination ...

items.description: Iranian state television confirmed on Sunday that newly appointed Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei was wounded during the ongoing conflict with the United States and Israel, referring to him as "janbaz" — a term meaning wounded by the enemy — in what Iranian media are calling the "Ramadan war." The disclosure came just hours after the Assembly of Experts officially announced his appointment on March 8, succeeding his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in the initial U.S.-Israeli strikes on February 28.[1][2][3]

items.title: UAE calls for de-escalation after 1,400 Iranian attacks

featured_image.name: UAE envoy to UN urges de-escalation of US-Israeli war with ...

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates on Monday called for an immediate de-escalation of the US-Israeli war with Iran and a return to negotiations, as the Gulf state disclosed it had been subjected to more than 1,400 Iranian drone and missile attacks since the conflict erupted on February 28.

"De-escalation, de-escalation, de-escalation. This is our position and we will continue to offer it," UAE Ambassador Jamal Jama al Musharakh told reporters during a press briefing at the United Nations in Geneva, according to Reuters.[1]

items.title: US intercepts Iran signal that may activate sleeper cells abroad

featured_image.name: Iran may be activating sleeper cells outside the country, alert says

items.description: Nearly two weeks into Operation Epic Fury, the joint US-Israeli air campaign that began on February 28, Iran's decentralized military doctrine is being put to its most severe test — and by several accounts, it is holding. Despite the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and senior military commanders, Iran has continued launching waves of ballistic missiles and drones at targets across the Middle East, raising questions about whether airpower alone can neutralize the Islamic Republic's war-fighting capacity.
